1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nf6 4.O-O Nxe4 5.strategy: The main line: strikes at e5 before Black can consolidate the extra pawn, and opens the e-file against a king still in the centre. Black can hardly take on d4, since the rook would pin the knight on e4 to the king, so the knight has to retreat or be supported.
Retreats the knight to safety and attacks the bishop in the same move. Black gives the extra pawn back for a safe, sound structure, the usual road to a solid game with early exchanges.

Prepares castling and avoids the early endgame of the main line, keeping the pieces on. The knight on e4 stays loose, though, so White gains time against it, and the extra pawn has to be returned anyway.

Asks the bishop at once, while the knight on e4 still holds the extra pawn. If the bishop retreats, Black reaches a main line of the Ruy Lopez with an active knight; if White takes on c6, Black recaptures with the d-pawn and keeps a sound game.
